rv.q: Her production, a triumph of storytelling and atmosphere, makes its own point.
A certain trepidation attends the West End transfer of Summer and Smoke, Tennessee Williams's portrait of a prim young Southern lady trembling with desire.
It is a pleasure to be able to report, therefore, that Rebecca Frecknall's boldly expressionist production – with its electrifying soundscape – galvanises the audience from the start.
It's hard to imagine 'Summer and Smoke' in better shape.

The Almeida’s acclaimed production of Tennessee Williams’ SUMMER AND SMOKE has transferred this week to the Duke of York’s Theatre for a limited West End season. Matthew Needham (John) and Patsy Ferran (Alma) in Summer & Smoke.

cn.t: Frecknall's acclaimed Almeida production of Williams' 1948 drama transfers to the West End with strong reviews, praised for its reinvention of the Southern Gothic tale of repressed desire and Ferran's performance as the trembling Alma.
